title: Understanding the organization and its context
requirement: The organization identifies the external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended results of its information security management system.

title: Needs and expectations of interested parties
requirement: The organization identifies interested parties and their information security requirements, including legal, regulatory and contractual obligations.

title: Scope of the ISMS
requirement: The boundaries and applicability of the information security management system are defined and documented as a scope statement.

title: Leadership and commitment
requirement: Top management demonstrates commitment by setting direction, providing resources, and integrating information security into business processes.

title: Information security policy
requirement: A documented information security policy is approved by top management, communicated within the organization, available to interested parties, and includes objectives and a commitment to meet requirements and to continually improve.

title: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
requirement: Roles and responsibilities for information security are assigned and communicated, including who reports on ISMS performance to top management.

title: Information security risk assessment
requirement: A defined and repeatable risk assessment process exists with risk acceptance criteria, identification of risks and risk owners, and analysis and evaluation of risk levels, with results documented.

title: Information security risk treatment
requirement: Risk treatment options are selected, necessary controls are determined, a Statement of Applicability is produced, and a risk treatment plan is approved by the risk owners.

title: Information security objectives and planning
requirement: Measurable information security objectives are set at relevant functions and levels, monitored, and supported by plans stating who does what, with which resources and by when.

title: Competence
requirement: The organization determines the competence needed for people affecting information security, ensures it through training or hiring, and retains evidence of competence.

title: Awareness
requirement: Personnel are aware of the security policy, their contribution to the ISMS, and the consequences of not following requirements.

title: Documented information
requirement: Required documents and records are identified, created and updated with proper identification, versioning, review and approval, and are controlled for access, distribution, retention and protection.

title: Operational planning and control
requirement: Processes needed to meet security requirements are planned, implemented and controlled, changes are managed, and outsourced processes are controlled.

title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
requirement: The organization defines what to monitor and measure, the methods, the timing, and who analyses the results, in order to evaluate security performance and ISMS effectiveness.

title: Internal audit
requirement: Internal audits of the ISMS are carried out at planned intervals under an audit programme by objective and impartial auditors, and results are reported to relevant management.

title: Management review
requirement: Top management reviews the ISMS at planned intervals considering defined inputs such as audit results, incidents and risk status, and documents decisions on improvements and changes.

title: Nonconformity and corrective action
requirement: When a nonconformity occurs the organization reacts, fixes it, analyses root causes, implements corrective actions, reviews their effectiveness, and keeps documented records.

title: Policies for information security
requirement: An information security policy and topic-specific policies are defined, approved by management, published, acknowledged by staff and reviewed at planned intervals or after significant changes.

title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
requirement: An inventory of information and associated assets is maintained and each asset has an assigned owner.

title: Acceptable use of information and assets
requirement: Rules for the acceptable use and handling of information and assets are documented and implemented.

title: Access control
requirement: Rules to control physical and logical access based on business and security needs are defined, documented and enforced, following need-to-know and least privilege.

title: Authentication information
requirement: Allocation and management of authentication information such as passwords is controlled, with guidance on password quality, secure handling and change when compromised.

title: Information security in supplier relationships
requirement: Processes exist to manage the information security risks associated with the use of suppliers and their products or services.

title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
requirement: Relevant security requirements are agreed with and documented in contracts with each supplier.

title: Information security incident management planning
requirement: Incident management processes, roles and responsibilities are defined and communicated, covering reporting, assessment, response and learning.

title: Response to information security incidents
requirement: Security incidents are responded to according to documented procedures, including containment, eradication, recovery and communication.

title: Information security during disruption
requirement: The organization plans how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during a disruption.

title: ICT readiness for business continuity
requirement: ICT readiness is planned, implemented, maintained and tested based on business continuity objectives and recovery requirements.

title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
requirement: Applicable legal, regulatory and contractual requirements for information security are identified, documented and kept up to date.

title: Privacy and protection of personal data
requirement: The organization identifies and meets requirements for the preservation of privacy and protection of personally identifiable information according to applicable laws.

title: Screening
requirement: Background verification checks on candidates are carried out before they join, in proportion to business needs, information classification and risks.

title: Information security awareness, education and training
requirement: Personnel receive appropriate security awareness, education and training, with regular updates of policies and procedures relevant to their job.

title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
requirement: Security responsibilities that remain valid after termination or change of employment are defined, enforced and communicated.

title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
requirement: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements reflecting the organization's needs are identified, documented, reviewed and signed by personnel and relevant parties.

title: Physical entry
requirement: Secure areas are protected by appropriate entry controls and access points, and visitors are managed.

title: Storage media
requirement: Storage media are managed through their life cycle of acquisition, use, transport and disposal according to the classification scheme.

title: User endpoint devices
requirement: Information stored on, processed by or accessible via user endpoint devices is protected through defined rules and configurations.

title: Privileged access rights
requirement: The allocation and use of privileged access rights is restricted, approved and managed.

title: Secure authentication
requirement: Secure authentication technologies and procedures, such as multi-factor authentication where needed, are implemented based on access restrictions.

title: Protection against malware
requirement: Protection against malware is implemented and supported by appropriate user awareness.

title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
requirement: Information about technical vulnerabilities is obtained, exposure is evaluated, and appropriate measures such as patching are taken in a timely way.

title: Information backup
requirement: Backup copies of information, software and systems are maintained and regularly tested in line with an agreed backup policy.

title: Logging
requirement: Logs recording activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events are produced, stored, protected and analysed.

title: Monitoring activities
requirement: Networks, systems and applications are monitored for anomalous behaviour, and appropriate action is taken to evaluate potential incidents.

title: Networks security
requirement: Networks and network devices are secured, managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.

title: Use of cryptography
requirement: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, are defined and implemented.

title: Secure development life cycle
requirement: Rules for the secure development of software and systems are established and applied.

title: Change management
requirement: Changes to information processing facilities and systems follow a change management procedure.
